title: HC Jeff Hafley - Oct 28 | Press Conference
headline: Both Jonah Savaiinaea and Kadyn Proctor are in the concussion protocol and sat out Wednesday's practice, with Jarrett Kingston taking the guard spot. Malik Willis's running was called a critical weapon ahead of the Patriots.
summary: Hafley said two players, referred to as 'Juju' (most likely Jonah Savaiinaea) and Kadyn Proctor, are in the concussion protocol. Both were symptomatic earlier in the week and did not practice. Everyone else on the 53-man roster was expected to practice. Jarrett Kingston, who replaced the injured guard in the last game, will be the guard in practice. On the trade deadline, he gave no specifics and said he and the GM talk about everything. He praised Malik Willis's decisiveness and said his ability to run was critical, including a huge fourth-down conversion and a draw. Jordyn Brooks was called a pro who played fast and physical, and rookie WR Caleb Douglas drew praise for clean alignment, run-game physicality and his red-zone work, with the hope of getting him the ball more. He also said a young TE (apparently Seydou Traore) earned 11 offensive snaps because of his special-teams physicality. Hafley was relaxed about Jacob Rodriguez's low tackle total, saying it depends on how offenses attack the defense. The next game is a divisional matchup with the Patriots, led by former coach Mike Vrabel. Hafley said he respects them, expects AJ Brown to be a focus of the game plan, and called special teams improved.

injuries.detail: Referred to as 'Juju'. In the concussion protocol, was symptomatic earlier in the week, and did not practice Wednesday. The name match is probable but not certain.
In the concussion protocol, was symptomatic earlier in the week, and did not practice Wednesday.

signals.note: He is stepping into an expanded OL role, which matters for Miami's run-blocking.
signals.quote: Kingston will be in today.

signals.claim: Willis's designed runs and scrambles will remain a meaningful part of the offense.
signals.note: His rushing gives him extra fantasy value, and the coach called the draw a weapon that is hard to defend.
signals.quote: it's a weapon that's hard to defend but it's critical

signals.note: This is a positive IDP read on his play and health.
signals.quote: I thought he looked fast last week. I thought he was flying to the ball.

signals.claim: Miami hopes to get Douglas the ball more going forward.
signals.note: He was clean with alignment and shifts, improved as a run blocker, and scored touchdowns, which supports a growing WR role.
signals.quote: hopefully we'll get a chance to get him the ball more.

signals.claim: Traore earned 11 offensive snaps and could keep a role on offense as he develops.
signals.note: Special-teams physicality is earning him offensive snaps, though the volume is small. The name match is inferred from 'Troy' and 'say do' in the captions.
signals.quote: we felt comfortable with him mentally and physically

signals.claim: Rodriguez's low tackle total reflects how offenses attacked the defense, not a decline in his play.
signals.note: Tackle volume for IDP managers depends on where opponents run and throw.
signals.quote: I thought he played a solid game.

signals.claim: Hafley supports aggressive, shot-taking play from DBs like Taaffe after his interception.
signals.note: This is a small IDP positive for a young DB who is being encouraged to gamble.
signals.quote: I want our players to be aggressive.

topics.detail: Hafley would not choose between listening on everything or standing pat. He said he and the GM discuss everything, much of it confidential, and that he loves this young team.
He sensed strong energy and focus coming off the win and the bye. He wants the team to stay even-keeled and aim to be better each day.
A strong run game pulls linebackers and safeties forward, which opens space for the pass and for explosive plays.
Hafley has high respect for Brown despite his slow start and expects him to be a focus of the game plan. He also praised Mike Vrabel and the physical, fundamental way the Patriots play.
He stressed teaching the young team the importance of division games and playing a full game, not just starting fast.
He thought special teams improved, with one hold penalty, good field position and solid coverage. A kicker hit some kickoffs well.

title: WATCH: Mike McCarthy Media Availability (Oct. 29)
headline: Steelers prepping for Browns in Week 8; McCarthy says Brisker is growing into the defense, red zone offense is a focus, and all recent IR players have a chance to return.
summary: McCarthy opened by praising the North Shore crowd and stressing the importance of protecting home games, with the Steelers undefeated at home. Asked about the 27th-ranked red zone offense, he said the team wants more touchdowns, needs to improve in both the run and pass game, and feels very good about this week's package against a tough situational defense. On the Browns winning all five of their games in the fourth quarter, he said late-game wins are the nature of today's NFL and that the Steelers have emphasized winning in the final series since their first team meeting. He highlighted Jaquan Brisker's availability, said he looks more comfortable in what the defense asks of him, noted the play-calling now reflects that, and said defensive communication is improving weekly, starting inside with Patrick Queen. On the offense's slow starts against Cleveland last time, he conceded it's a season-long issue they work on daily but gave no specifics. Asked about a receiver named Marquez, whom Rodgers wants to see on the field, he only asked for hard practice every day and noted his history with Rodgers. He said he doesn't see any of the recent IR placements as clearly season-ending and believes they all have a chance to return, without naming anyone.

injuries.detail: McCarthy said all players recently placed on injured reserve have a chance to return this season; no names or timelines given.

signals.claim: Brisker will remain a near every-down safety as he grows more comfortable in the scheme.
signals.note: He played nearly every defensive snap and the coach says play calls are reflecting his comfort, which is good for IDP value.
signals.quote: you see him more and more comfortable for what we're asking him to do

signals.claim: Queen is the center of defensive communication that is improving each week.
signals.note: His role as the defensive signal-caller supports his continued heavy usage for IDP purposes.
signals.quote: the communication really throughout our whole defense is, is getting better each and every week

topics.detail: Steelers rank 27th in red zone offense; McCarthy wants more touchdowns, says run and pass both need work, and likes this week's package.
McCarthy acknowledged the slow offense for much of the last Browns game and called it a daily work item, with no specific adjustments named.
Browns are 5-for-5 in fourth-quarter wins; McCarthy says winning the final series has been a team theme since the first meeting.
Recent IR players all have a chance to return, per the coach.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald On The Quenton Nelson Trade, Preparing For Week 8
headline: Quenton Nelson starts at left guard Monday night with Grey Zabel moving to right guard, and Anthony Bradford loses his starting job. Charles Cross, Rashid Shaheed and Velus Jones Jr. are not practicing, and Cross is not going to IR.
summary: Macdonald opened by welcoming the newly acquired guard Quenton Nelson, who will practice today. He said the line played its best game of the season Sunday night, and that the trade is no commentary on the existing linemen. Nelson will play left guard and Grey Zabel will slide to right guard, where he has plenty of experience. Macdonald said the team expects Nelson to play Monday night and called that realistic even with only a couple of practices. He was candid that benching Anthony Bradford is not an easy situation, since Bradford earned a starting-level role, but said he will stay ready. Charles Cross is 'coming along great' but will not practice today, and for now he is not going on injured reserve. Josh Jones is the third tackle. Rashid Shaheed and Velus Jones Jr. are not expected to practice, while Drake Thomas will be out there today. On the Bears, Macdonald praised their identity in all three phases and the league-leading rush offense under Ben Johnson. He also noted Montez Sweat's return and the Jeffrey Simmons addition, and he declined to explain why Byron Murphy was stood up on some pass rushes.

injuries.detail: Not practicing today but 'coming along great.' Macdonald said he is not going on injured reserve as of now.

signals.note: The shuffled line needs time to gel, but Zabel's past right-side experience should ease the transition.

signals.note: A return to practice is a good sign for the linebacker's availability against Chicago.

topics.detail: Macdonald said the line played its best game Sunday, and that the Nelson trade is not a criticism of the current linemen. Chemistry will need work after a few shifts, but he expects the group to mesh quickly.

He described the Bears as having a clear identity in all three phases and the league's top rushing offense, built on physical runners, a good line, strong tight ends and receivers who block. He praised Ben Johnson's use of personnel and noted their trick plays.
Montez Sweat is returning after missing the season, and Jeffrey Simmons has been added, which Macdonald said Seattle must plan for. He said the Bears are strong on third down under Coach Allen.

Seattle will stay in its 'wheelhouse' scheme instead of changing each week, relying on four-down fronts and edge defenders who play decisively and violently. Macdonald said the team's rules matter more than any trick-play worry.
Macdonald called midseason acquisitions under GM John Schneider 'almost a prerequisite' and said he judges each move by whether it moves the needle for the team.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Titans traded DT Jeffery Simmons; Keldric Faulk and Oluwafemi Oladejo get more D-line snaps, while Carnell Tate sat out practice and Tyjae Spears and 'Tony' may be hurt too.
summary: Saleh opened with injuries: Carnell Tate, "Tony" and "Taj" did not practice, and John Franklin-Myers should be limited. Most of the session was about the trade of Jeffery Simmons, which he called shocking, "unfortunately necessary" and the hard part of the business. He said the 1-6 team couldn't close out games and a team eventually offered a package the Titans couldn't turn down. He said the trade was about accelerating the rebuild through an influx of young talent and had nothing to do with Cam Ward. He pointed to more opportunity on the defensive line, naming Keldric Faulk on third-down passing situations and Femi (Oluwafemi Oladejo), and said the backups believe they are capable starters. He said Simmons had been battling something he wouldn't detail and had still been playing well for his condition. He noted that opposing offenses will no longer slide protection toward Simmons, so the coaches have more film work to do. He named JC Latham, Peter Skoronski, Calvin Ridley, Cam Ward and Amani Hooker among the leaders who will fill the void. He praised owner Amy Adams Strunk's support and gave a brief positive scouting report on Jonah Laulu, who came in the deal. He said the team will keep working this week ahead of Cincinnati on Sunday.

topics.detail: Saleh said the Simmons trade was unfortunate but necessary. The 1-6 Titans haven't been closing games, and a team offered a package they couldn't refuse. He compared it to trades by Cleveland, Detroit (Goff) and Seattle (Russell) and said it accelerates the rebuild.
Saleh said Simmons has been battling something he wouldn't detail, that his current best is better than most players', and that he expects him to finish strong. He said the bye week will help.

Offenses used to slide protection toward Simmons, which made it easy to know where to attack. Without him the coaches have to study protections and slides on tape and put players in the best position.
Saleh named JC Latham, Peter Skoronski, Calvin Ridley, Cam Ward and Amani Hooker as leaders, along with a defensive line he called full of alphas.
Saleh praised Amy Adams Strunk's support and said she backs developing the roster, but he acknowledged winning is what counts.
Saleh called him a big, athletic defensive tackle who fits what the Titans want and said they look forward to getting a look at him.
